get.description: Verifies `state`, requires the `activity:read_all` scope, exchanges the code for tokens, stores the athlete with encrypted tokens and enqueues the initial backfill. If the login carried an allowlisted `return_to`, the browser is redirected (303) there with `connected=1`, or with `connect_error=<reason>` once the state itself is valid.

400.description: Bad state, denied access, missing scope or bad code

get.description: Redirects the browser to Strava's authorize page with a signed, expiring `state`. An optional `return_to` that exactly matches `OAUTH_RETURN_TO_ALLOWLIST` is signed into the state; after the callback the browser is sent there. Any other value is ignored.

parameters.description: Where to send the browser after connecting (allowlisted URLs only)
parameters.name: return_to

schema.description: Where to send the browser after connecting (allowlisted URLs only)
schema.title: Return To

get.summary: Readiness: PostgreSQL and Redis are reachable

get.description: Stored activities of all active athletes (or one, with `athlete_id`), newest first. Soft-deleted activities are excluded. Pages are keyset-based: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. Rows inserted while paging never shift or repeat a page.

parameters.description: Start date ≥ this (UTC if no offset)
parameters.name: from

schema.description: Start date ≥ this (UTC if no offset)
schema.title: From

parameters.description: Start date < this (UTC if no offset)
parameters.name: to

schema.description: Start date < this (UTC if no offset)
schema.title: To

get.description: One stored activity of an active athlete, by its Strava id. Unknown and soft-deleted activities are 404.
The language (`/lang`) and profanity level (`/swear`) the chat chose, or null.

put.description: Idempotent: the same body twice stores one row. A field left out keeps its stored value; at least one is required.
put.summary: Store the settings of a chat

get.description: Check-ins in `from`..`to` (inclusive, local days); default: the last 12 weeks.

Current and longest streak (consecutive days with a check-in that is not `skipped`) and adherence over `from`..`to` (default: the current ISO week and the three before it). Adherence = planned days done / planned days, where each ISO week plans `days_per_week` of the active program, capped by its days inside the range minus sick/injured days; done + partial days count as done (ADR 0020).

put.description: Upsert by date: `201` when it created the check-in, `200` when it replaced it. The same request twice stores one row. `body_weight_kg` is also written to body metrics for that date; leaving it out later does not delete that body metric.

get.description: Local foods only (manual entries and cached Open Food Facts products): case-insensitive substring of name or brand, or an exact barcode. Favorites first, then by name.

post.description: A manual food with per-100 g values. Unknown macros may be null.

get.description: Exactly one of `barcode` or `q`. A barcode already stored is answered locally (`remote=cached`). Otherwise Open Food Facts is asked (3 s budget) and every usable product (barcode, name and kcal known) is cached in the food list. If Open Food Facts is slow or down the answer still comes, with local matches only and `remote=unavailable`.

400.description: Neither or both of barcode and q

get.summary: Look a food up in Open Food Facts

patch.description: Changes only the fields sent. Editing a cached Open Food Facts food turns it into a `manual` one, so a later lookup never overwrites the edit. Logged entries use the food's current values.

400.description: A required field set to null

get.description: Entries of one day (default: today, UTC), in meal order, then as logged.

put.description: Upsert by the client-generated `client_id`: `201` when it created the entry, `200` when an entry with this id already existed and was updated. Retrying the same request stores one entry. The food's kcal and macros are copied into the entry, so editing the food later does not change past days.

get.description: Profile, targets and today's BMR estimate.

put.description: Replaces the profile. A `kcal_target` below the estimated BMR is accepted and comes back with a `warning`.

get.description: One day (default: today, UTC). All energy figures are estimates: BMR by Mifflin-St Jeor from the profile and the latest body weight on or before the day, times the everyday-activity multiplier (1.2 / 1.375 / 1.55) without exercise; exercise from synced activities (`raw.calories`, else for rides `raw.kilojoules` ≈ kcal, else unknown). Balance = intake - (baseline + known exercise). Unknown inputs are flagged, never guessed. Days are UTC days.
get.summary: Daily nutrition summary and energy balance

get.description: One summary per day in `from`..`to` (both inclusive, at most 92 days) plus totals. Defaults to the current ISO week (Monday to Sunday, UTC). All energy figures are estimates: BMR by Mifflin-St Jeor from the profile and the latest body weight on or before the day, times the everyday-activity multiplier (1.2 / 1.375 / 1.55) without exercise; exercise from synced activities (`raw.calories`, else for rides `raw.kilojoules` ≈ kcal, else unknown). Balance = intake - (baseline + known exercise). Unknown inputs are flagged, never guessed. Days are UTC days.
get.summary: Nutrition summary per day for a range

get.description: Count, distance, moving time and elevation for activities whose start date falls in `from`..`to` (both inclusive, UTC days), the same totals per sport type (sorted by sport type), and the longest activity: the one with the greatest distance, the newest on a tie. An empty range gives zeros, an empty `by_sport` and a null `longest`. Defaults to the last 12 weeks. Soft-deleted activities are excluded.

Count, distance, moving time and elevation per ISO week (Monday start, UTC) for activities whose start date falls in `from`..`to` (both inclusive). Weeks without activities are returned with zeros. Defaults to the last 12 weeks. Soft-deleted activities are excluded.
Latest backfill and incremental run per active athlete, webhook intake and retry counts, current Strava rate-limit usage, and the circuit breaker state of every process that talks to Strava.
Oldest first; `from`/`to` inclusive.

put.summary: Record body weight for a day

get.description: Built-in and custom exercises by name. `q` matches name or slug (case-insensitive substring), `muscle` the primary or a secondary muscle, `equipment` any of the given.

post.description: The slug is derived from the name; a name whose slug exists already is `409`.

get.description: Per workout that logged the exercise (oldest first): best set, best e1RM (Epley, 1-12 reps), working volume. `from`/`to` are inclusive UTC dates.
Plates to load on each side for `target` kg, from `GYM_BAR_KG` and the `GYM_PLATES` inventory. If the target cannot be made, the nearest lower weight and the difference.
Every program, newest first, without days.

post.description: A program with its days (in order) and planned exercises (in order). The program generator's preview (`POST /programs/generate`) has a `program` field that can be sent here unchanged. New programs are inactive.

400.description: A planned exercise does not exist

get.description: The one active program with its days, or `404` when none is active.

The program day that is up next, in rotation: the day after the one the latest workout followed (wrapping around), the first day if none, or the day of a still-open workout. Planned exercises come with the double-progression suggestion (ADR 0018). `404` when no program is active.
get.summary: Next day of the active program

post.description: Deterministic, rule-based program from the exercise library: template by days per week (2-3 full body, 4 upper/lower, 3 or 6 push/pull/legs), exercises by movement pattern and equipment, sets/reps/rest by goal, trimmed to `session_minutes`. Nothing is saved: `program` is a ready body for `POST /v1/training/programs`.

delete.description: Deletes the program and its days; logged workouts stay.

get.description: One program with its days and planned exercises.

put.description: Replaces name, goal, weeks and all days. Logged workouts stay; their link to a replaced program day becomes null.

400.description: A planned exercise does not exist

post.description: Makes this the only active program (idempotent).

get.description: Standing records per exercise: heaviest weight per rep count, best e1RM and best session volume, with the workout that set them.
Working sets and kg (reps x weight) per ISO week and primary muscle. `from`/`to` are inclusive UTC dates; default the last 12 weeks.
Newest first, keyset-paginated (ADR 0009): pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`.

put.description: Starts a workout, free or from a program day, under a client-generated `client_id` (ADR 0017): `201` when it started the workout, `200` when a workout with this id already exists (a retry, a double tap or a check-in edit), returned unchanged: the first start wins, whatever the repeat's body says. The response lists the day's planned exercises with the last performance of each (working sets of the most recent other workout that logged it).

delete.description: Deletes the workout and its sets.

get.description: Sets, volume, records hit and (for a program day) the plan with last performance.

post.description: Sets `ended_at` (default now); an empty workout can be finished. Finishing again keeps the first `ended_at` (idempotent) but updates `notes` when sent.

delete.description: Idempotent: deleting a set that is not there is also `204`.

put.description: Upsert by the client-generated `client_id` (ADR 0017): the first call creates the set (`201`), a retry or a correction with the same id updates that same set (`200`, same body for the same input). Retries and double taps never create a second set. An id already used in another workout is `409`.

get.description: Strava calls this once when the subscription is created. Echoes `hub.challenge` when `hub.mode=subscribe` and `hub.verify_token` matches `STRAVA_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN`.

post.description: Validates the event, stores it once (deduplicated on subscription, object, aspect and event time) and enqueues `process_webhook_event`. Always answers 200 for a well-formed event, including duplicates and events for another subscription, so Strava does not retry. No Strava call happens here.

400.description: Body is not a valid Strava event
